headline: Bill Gates says AI needs safety rules like planes, cars and medicines, but calls fears that it could end humanity overblown.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 2: an opinion that repeats Gates's calls of 27 and 29 Sep already carried, with no policy action and no dates for the quoted remarks.
importance_line: What changed: a leading tech figure again urges AI safety rules, which bears on how the public is protected from misuse, how lawmakers weigh new laws and what AI companies must accept, but it is one person's opinion, no new law follows, and the dates of the quoted remarks are not given.
summary: India Today reports that Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates wrote on X that AI needs safeguards like those that cover planes, cars and medicines, which "won't eliminate every harm" but can help stop bad actors misusing it. In a CNN interview he said talk that all of humanity is at risk can get "overblown" while still rating AI as more dangerous than cars, planes or drugs, repeating a call for required safeguards he made on NBC on 27 Sep 2026 (our 28 Sep edition).
notes: Read India Today in full. Repeats Gates's calls of 27 Sep (NBC) and 29 Sep (New York Times), carried in our 28 and 30 Sep editions; the X post itself may be new but is undated in the article.
